summary: Built a real block-level filesystem snapshot/rollback capability for /srv/data on node1 using device-mapper dm-snapshot (no LVM package or repo access was available, so an origin+COW loop-device setup was wired manually). Demonstrated a full modify-then-restore cycle verified by sha256 checksum equality, made the setup persist across reboot via a systemd unit, and completed the mandatory single-node restart verification with a changed boot_id and confirmed post-restart data/service recovery.
actions_performed: Surveyed node1: RHEL 7.9, xfs root on a plain partition (no LVM), no yum repos reachable, but device-mapper/dmsetup present
Created loopback-backed origin (1GiB) and COW (512MiB) sparse image files under /var/lib/snapstore
Created a dm 'snapshot-origin' target (data-origin) over the origin loop device, formatted it xfs, and mounted it at /srv/data
Populated baseline application data (config file, records.csv, marker file) and recorded a sha256 manifest
Froze the filesystem and created a persistent dm 'snapshot' target (data-snap) capturing that exact baseline state
Modified /srv/data (deleted records.csv, corrupted the config file, added a stray file) to simulate an accidental change

Mounted the snapshot read-only and restored /srv/data to be byte-identical to the pre-modification snapshot (removed files absent from the snapshot, cp -a'd the rest); verified via sha256 diff = IDENTICAL

Wrote /usr/local/sbin/srv-data-setup.sh and enabled systemd unit srv-data.service (WantedBy=local-fs.target) to reattach loop devices, recreate data-origin, and remount /srv/data automatically at boot
Captured pre-restart baseline evidence: boot_id, uptime, mount state, file checksums, dm device list
Triggered 'shutdown -r now' in the background so the acknowledgement returned before disconnect; polled until node1 was reachable again
Confirmed boot_id changed (d7a80301-53d3-4cc8-bd41-1293f67d0769 -> 3cc9d27e-c7e7-4831-b98d-ba38386c470f) and uptime reset to ~16s, proving an actual restart occurred
Verified post-restart recovery: srv-data.service active (exited/success), /srv/data auto-remounted via data-origin, and file checksums matched the original baseline exactly

Created a fresh dm-snapshot (data-snap) of the recovered baseline state so /srv/data remains actively snapshot-protected going forward, and did a final checksum diff confirming it still matches the original baseline manifest
